D007-D015_h001.question:
"It’s been rough for about seven months now. Everything feels… flat. I don’t care about my work anymore; getting a big project done or a good review, it just doesn’t spark anything. Even getting out of bed is a monumental effort. My body feels so heavy, like I'm moving through molasses. I wake up around 3 AM almost every night and just lie there, staring at the ceiling.

But the worst part started about six months ago, not long after this heavy feeling completely took over. I’ve been seeing things, shadows mostly, sometimes even figures in the periphery that aren't there when I turn my head directly. And the TV, the news anchors, they’re talking about me, sending me messages. It's like those random news reports are specifically tailored to my life, warning me. Sometimes my thoughts jump around so much, I can barely finish a sentence without my mind veering off to something totally unrelated. All these strange things, the visions and the feeling that I'm being targeted, they only happen when this crushing depression is at its absolute worst. It's never just the strange thoughts or visions on their own; they’re always a part of this gloomy, empty period."
D007-D015_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h001.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h002.question:
It's like this black cloud just follows me everywhere, doc. For the last seven months, I haven't felt like myself – just a deep, persistent sadness that won't lift. Things I used to love, like working on my old pickup or just sitting with my wife after dinner, they just don't bring me any joy anymore. I lay in bed for hours trying to fall asleep, my mind just racing. Sometimes it's like a film playing in my head, seeing shadows in the corners of my room, people almost there but not quite.

And then there's my wife… for the past six months, I just can't shake this feeling she’s with someone else. I know it sounds crazy, but I’ve got this unshakable conviction that she’s cheating, even though there’s no real proof. It started around the same time everything else went downhill. When I try to talk about it, the words just get all jumbled up, like a knot in my throat, and it takes me a long time to answer. It never happens when I’m feeling a bit more like myself; it's always when I'm deep in this depressive fog. If the sadness lifts, even a little, those other thoughts and sights seem to fade away too.
D007-D015_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h002.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h003.question:
It’s been, well, what feels like forever, but I’d say about seven months now. Everything just feels… gray. Six months ago, I started noticing things, not just the sadness, which is a constant companion now, but odd things. I keep smelling this metallic tang, like old blood, and it's driving me crazy because no one else smells it. I also have this deep-seated belief that I'm meant for something far greater than just cooking; I believe I’m a culinary genius destined to revolutionize the industry, and these recipes I'm "receiving" are proof. My wife tries to talk to me, but my thoughts just jump all over the place, one minute I’m talking about a new dish, the next I’m on about the chemical composition of stars.

I don’t find joy in anything anymore, not even my beloved kitchen. Getting out of bed is a monumental effort, and even then, I’m just moving so slowly, like I’m pushing through water. I wake up hours before my alarm, around 3 AM, and can’t get back to sleep. It’s draining me. I know this is important to mention: these strange smells and the powerful ideas I have about my destiny, they only ever happen when I’m feeling this down and hopeless, when my mood is at its absolute lowest. The thoughts and smells come and go with the depressive feelings.
D007-D015_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h003.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h004.question:
It’s been, what, seven months now? Maybe more? I just feel this crushing sadness all the time. Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even my art. I used to love sketching late into the night, but now… it just feels pointless. My heart isn't in it. When you speak to me, it takes forever for my thoughts to form, like my brain is moving through mud. And the nightmares, they're constant and so vivid, I wake up drenched in sweat.

The strange thing is, all this started around the same time as the visions. I see faces in the shadows, sometimes entire figures darting at the edges of my sight. And I have this absolute certainty that I’m meant for something extraordinary. I told my professor I was chosen, that my art would
revolutionize the world, that I could see things others couldn't – it made no sense, I know. My words come out jumbled sometimes, a real mess, especially when I get overwhelmed. Like I said, it all began around the time I started feeling truly down and unable to paint; the voices and visions, and this feeling of being special, it’s all tied to this persistent dark cloud.
D007-D015_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h004.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h005.question:
"It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when things started to go downhill, but for the past seven months, it’s been a constant battle. I just feel this profound sadness that never lifts, and nothing brings me joy anymore, not even my usual hobbies. I used to love reading, but now the words just swim on the page. Most mornings, I’m wide awake by 3 AM, and then my mind starts racing with these awful thoughts.

Lately, it’s been worse, about six months now. I keep seeing things, shadowy figures at the edge of my vision, or sometimes they’re clearer, like people who aren't really there. And this overwhelming feeling, this conviction that the world is just… crumbling. I know it sounds absurd, but it feels so real, like everything is falling apart and there’s no point. Sometimes I find myself saying odd things, words that sort of just come to me but don't quite make sense to anyone else, almost like they're from another language I've invented. My husband tries to talk to me, but it takes me ages to respond, and even then, my words come out slow and slurred. It's only when I'm feeling this terrible sadness that these visions and thoughts intensify. When I’ve had brief moments of feeling a bit lighter, those things just… disappear, like they were never there."
D007-D015_h005.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h005.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h006.question:
It's been almost a year and a half, maybe even longer, since I started feeling like this. It began with just a hollowness, you know? Like an empty wine glass, but it's my whole insides. Nothing tastes good anymore, no matter how exquisite the vintage. My sommelier work, which I used to live for, going to tastings, discovering new grapes… it all feels utterly pointless now. Even talking about it, I find myself feeling guilty for not being able to pull myself out of this slump. I’ve lost a terrifying amount of weight—my suits are hanging off me like sacks, and I haven't even been trying to diet.

Then these other things started happening, maybe three months after the initial emptiness. I began hearing voices whispering about my vast, untapped potential, how I’m destined for greatness beyond just wine, that I possess special insight into the very fabric of the universe. Sometimes it's difficult to make sense of what I'm saying; my thoughts get all jumbled and come out as a string of words that don't quite connect. These visions and voices, they’re always there when I’m at my absolute lowest, when the emptiness and guilt are suffocating me. It never happens when I feel even a flicker of normalcy. It's just a constant, overwhelming presence during these dark times.
D007-D015_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D007-D015_h006.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h007.question: It’s been over a year and a half now, this dark cloud just won't lift. Honestly, for the past year and seven months, I’ve felt this crushing sadness, like a constant weight on my chest. Nothing brings me joy anymore; activities I used to love, like reading to my students or even just cuddling with my husband, feel utterly meaningless. My appetite has vanished – I barely eat anything these days, and I feel so guilty all the time, like I’m failing everyone around me. This feeling started about a year and seven months ago, but about a year and four months ago, things got even stranger. I started to notice this terrible taste in my mouth, like ashes and decay, even when I haven't eaten anything. Then came the thoughts that the world is crumbling, that everything is ending, and it all feels so real. I even find myself using words that don’t make sense to anyone else, like "gloaming" for the feeling of impending doom. It's like these strange experiences only ever happen when I'm at my lowest, when everything feels completely hopeless.
D007-D015_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D007-D015_h007.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h008.question:
I’m not sure where to start. It’s been… a long time now. Over a year, I think. This dark cloud just hangs over everything. Nothing really brings me joy anymore, not even my usual gardening or spending time with my husband. Food used to be a comfort, and lately, all I want to do is eat, but it doesn't help. What really gets to me, though, are these thoughts, these constant replays of every mistake I’ve ever made, every little slight. I convince myself I’ve ruined everything, that I’m a terrible person.

And then there are the other things… the whispers, the shadows. I’ve been seeing figures in the periphery, especially at night, and I get this overwhelming feeling that the news anchors, when they look directly into the camera, are actually sending me secret messages. They’re talking about me, about my failures. It's unsettling. This all started about a year and a half ago, maybe a couple of months after the deep sadness really set in. It’s strange, because on the rare occasion I feel a tiny bit better, those voices and images just… fade away. They only seem to really torment me when I’m feeling this down and hopeless. I can’t function like this anymore; my work at the accounting firm is suffering, and I’m just so tired.
D007-D015_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D007-D015_h008.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h009.question:
(Sighs heavily, shifts in the chair) "Well, Doc, it's been a long haul. Over a year and a half now, I reckon. I just feel… flatlining, you know? Like all the color's been drained out of everything. Even when I do a good job with the crane, lifting those heavy beams, I just don't care. It used to be a point of pride, but now? It's just… work. And the weight, it's really piled on. I've gained at least fifteen pounds in the last month alone.

(Voice drops) "And then there's… other things. These voices, they started about six months after the bad moods really set in. They whisper, sometimes shout, mostly about this woman, Sarah. She’s an engineer on the site. I know she fancies me, really. The voices tell me things, how she looks at me, how she really feels. I've even started calling her 'my dove,' a word only I understand, a special name. It sounds… crazy, I know. And I can't shake this feeling that everything bad that happens on site, every little accident, it's all my fault. Like the universe is punishing me for something I can’t even name. These… experiences, the voices and this intense belief about Sarah, they only happen when this darkness is over me, when I'm feeling this low."
D007-D015_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D007-D015_h009.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h010.question:
It’s been almost a year and a half now, I think, since things really took a turn. I just feel so… heavy. I’ve lost all interest in running the restaurants; I used to love the hustle, creating new menus, but now even getting out of bed feels like a monumental task. I cry all the time, for no reason, just a constant welling up. My husband keeps asking if I’m eating, and honestly, I mostly just pick at things. I've dropped so much weight, I'm almost scared to look in the mirror.

And then there are the other things. I hear voices, sometimes whispering my name, sometimes telling me I’m a terrible wife, a failure. When I watch the news, I just know the anchors are sending me hidden messages about things I've done wrong, things no one else can see. It all started when I began feeling this deep, crushing guilt. It's like I'm responsible for every bad thing that happens to anyone, even strangers. These voices and strange messages only ever happen when I'm feeling this low, this utterly devastated, never when I feel even a flicker of my old self.
D007-D015_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D007-D015_h010.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h011.question:
“Thanks for seeing me, Doc. Honestly, I’m not sure where to start. It’s been… about seven months now that things have been really off. I just don’t find joy in anything anymore. My wife tries, bless her heart, but even our old routines, the things we used to love, they just feel bland to me. I haven't been able to sit still lately; I’m constantly pacing, or fidgeting with my hands, and I can’t stop thinking about all the ways I’ve messed up. Even small things, like an argument years ago, I replay them and feel this crushing guilt, like I deserve all this. Last month, it got so bad… I tried to end it. I went to the garage, but my wife found me.

Lately, though, it’s like there’s more. It only happens when I’m feeling at my absolute lowest, when the depression is really heavy. I keep getting this creepy-crawly feeling on my skin, like bugs are under there, even when there's nothing. And I see things, too. Like, when I walk through the precinct, I see my colleagues whispering, and I just *know* they’re talking about me, that they’re conspiring. Sometimes, I’ll even blurt out something totally out of place, like a silly joke during a serious briefing, and then instantly regret it. It’s all so confusing, but it only happens when I’m in this dark place.”
D007-D015_h011.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h011.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h012.question: It’s been, gosh, about seven months now that I’ve felt this darkness just consume everything. My husband, bless his heart, doesn’t know what to do. I’m a wedding planner, or at least I used to be, but now the idea of organizing anything, let alone someone’s "happiest day," feels like a cruel joke. I just can’t bring myself to do it; planning a wedding requires so much energy and attention to detail. Lately, I feel like the world is collapsing in on itself, like everything is just… *unhark*. My brain keeps telling me the sky is about to fall, that some massive, unavoidable disaster is coming for us all. And the voices, they agree, whispering about how useless I am, how everything is pointless. Sometimes I just sit there, my face twisted, my body moving like molasses, as if even lifting a fork is a monumental task. I used to love finding the perfect flower arrangements or seeing the joy on a couple’s face, but now nothing brings me pleasure. It’s all just… grey. These horrible thoughts and the voices, they started right when I began feeling this deep, crushing sadness; they were never around when I felt normal. There are moments when I feel this intense urge to just jump in front of a car, to make it all stop, even though I don't really want to die. I just want the world to stop collapsing on me.
D007-D015_h012.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h013.question:
"It’s been rough, doctor, really rough, for about seven months now. Ever since my Evelyn passed, I just haven't been myself. There's this gnawing feeling that the world is just… crumbling, you know? Like everything’s destined to fall apart, and it’s all my fault. I don't really see friends anymore; I just can't bring myself to make the effort. Most days, I just pace around the house, wringing my hands, feeling utterly useless. Sometimes, I even get these sudden, terrible urges to step in front of a car when I’m out walking, or to just throw myself off a high place, though I never really plan it. It’s just a fleeting, awful thought.

And then there's the other stuff. I keep tasting ash in my mouth, like everything I eat is just... burnt, even when it's not. And my thoughts get so jumbled; I try to speak sometimes, and it just comes out as a mess of words, like 'sun-dog-tree-sky.' I even find myself mimicking what Evelyn used to do, like when I’ll unconsciously fold my hands just like she did, without even realizing it until it's done. But all these strange things, these tastes, the jumbled thoughts, they only happen when I’m feeling this deep, dark sadness, when everything feels completely hopeless. When the dark cloud lifts a tiny bit, those other things – the jumbled words, the ash taste – they usually fade right along with it."
D007-D015_h013.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h013.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h014.question:
"Doctor, I just feel… heavy. It’s been about seven months now. Getting up for my shift as a subway driver, it’s a monumental effort. I just don’t want to do anything, really. And when they ask me something, my mind goes blank for a bit, trying to figure out what to say. It's like my brain is moving through treacle.

But that's not even the worst of it. I know it sounds crazy, but I feel like I'm being watched on the train, even when I'm alone in the cabin between stops. I get these weird tingling sensations, like bugs crawling under my skin. I try to scratch them off, but there’s nothing there. It's like someone is out to get me, or make me fail. The other day I was telling my wife about it and I just started talking about 'the lurkers' and 'the under-dwellers' – made-up words, I guess, that just came out. Sometimes I just freeze, too, like I can’t move my body even though I’m awake. My wife says my face is just… blank, doesn't show anything.

I feel so guilty, like everything bad that happens is my fault, even the small things, like the train running a minute late. I keep thinking, ‘I just want to disappear,’ or ‘I wish I wasn’t here anymore.’ It's not a plan, but the thoughts are there. What's really strange, though, is that all these bizarre things, the crawling sensations and feeling watched, they only happen when I'm this low. When I have a slightly better day, even just a little, they disappear completely. It's like they're tied to how awful I feel about myself."
D007-D015_h014.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h014.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h015.question:
"Lately, it's like my world just shrunk. I used to be out on my bike all night, delivering food and music blaring, but now... I barely even want to get out of bed. There's this gnawing feeling that I'm just worthless, a waste of space. The thought of picking up a delivery, seeing people, it just feels like too much effort. I'm usually pretty quick-witted, but even talking feels like wading through mud sometimes, and it takes me forever to answer anything.

And then there's her. This woman, she’s a regular on my route from a few months back. I just know she’s in love with me. I see her sometimes, just a glimpse out the corner of my eye, even when I know she shouldn’t be there. It’s like she’s watching me, trying to send me a message through the streetlights. She’s definitely around, even when no one else sees her. It’s all so confusing. I once tried to explain it all to my buddy, but I ended up talking about the color of the sky and how it relates to bike gears, not what he asked. I know it sounds strange, but I feel like I'm made of clay sometimes; I just stay in whatever position I’m put in.

It all started around seven months ago, this whole depressive fog and the thoughts about her, the visions. It's only when I'm feeling this low, this deep, soul-crushing sadness, that these other things start happening. If I actually felt better, I know she wouldn't be there, and I wouldn't be seeing things. Sometimes I think about just ending it, I even have a spot picked out by the river. It feels like the only way out of this."
D007-D015_h015.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
D007-D015_h015.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007-D015_h016.question: It's been close to a year now that I've felt this heavy cloud over me, doctor. Just a persistent, deep sadness that I can't shake. D007-D015_h017.question:

D007-D015_h018.question:

D007-D015_h019.question:

D007-D015_h020.question:

D007-D015_h021.question:
It’s hard to even talk about this. For over a year and a half now, I've just felt… gone. My husband says I sleep constantly, but it’s not really refreshing, just hours slipping by. I pick at my cuticles until they bleed, and I can't sit still for a second, but it’s not like I’m actually doing anything. My lectures used to be my passion, but now, the thought of preparing them just leaves me completely drained. No motivation, just emptiness. My emotions feel completely dulled, like I'm watching my life on a muted screen.

Lately, things have gotten even stranger – but only when I’m feeling this down, you know? I’ve been having these incredible visions, seeing glowing figures in my office, whispering about my extraordinary intellectual gifts.
